title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-06
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains, with one separately marked recent-search addition
ranking_explanation: The 14 repositories present on GitHub Trending today are ordered by the displayed stars-today count. livliv-dev/player is appended as a recent (created 2026-11-04), actively maintained candidate after its first-party README was reviewed; it was not on the Trending page, so its daily gain is unavailable and it is not ranked against the Trending entries.
global_caveat: A one-day Trending count is a short-horizon popularity signal, not a measure of adoption or project quality. Current star totals and default-branch commits were corroborated with GitHub REST API responses; the fresh candidate has no comparable Trending daily gain.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-06 17:32 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-06 through 2026-11-06. Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains; one recent Search candidate is appended without a daily gain figure.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Today's strongest surge is around practical agent workflows: Cloudflare's security-audit skill, Matt Pocock's engineering skills, and NVIDIA's Auto Ontology lead the daily gains. Google skills add to the agent-skills signal, while editors, frameworks, and infrastructure repositories show the wider breadth of the day's list.

sections.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
sections.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings.
sections.why_notable: The largest daily star gain in the captured Trending list, and a concrete, staged security-audit workflow with separate candidate verification and structured findings.
sections.unique_caveat: GitHub reports its latest push as 2026-09-14; today's large star gain is not matched by a recent push.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Composable agent skills for practical software engineering, maintained from the author's agents directory.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain; the README stresses small, editable, composable skills that work across models rather than imposing a single end-to-end process.

sections.title: NVIDIA/auto-ontology
sections.description: A Python framework for semantic, graph-based reasoning layers that ground LLM and agent workflows in data.
sections.why_notable: Third-highest daily gain and a distinctive data/ML theme: it aims to give agents business definitions, lineage, and validated context, exposed through MCP, CLI, and API.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says external contributions are currently not being accepted.

sections.title: google/skills
sections.description: Agent skills for Google products and technologies, including Google Cloud.
sections.why_notable: One of today's clearest agent-skills signals, with installation through the skills.sh ecosystem and product-specific workflows.

sections.title: lz4/lz4
sections.description: An extremely fast lossless compression algorithm and command-line utility.
sections.why_notable: Its 313-star daily gain makes a long-established performance primitive a notable counterpoint to the day's agent-centric projects.

sections.title: microsoft/vscode
sections.why_notable: A top daily gain for a mature developer tool, reinforcing that editor infrastructure is still drawing strong community attention.

sections.title: zed-industries/zed
sections.description: A high-performance multiplayer code editor from the creators of Atom and Tree-sitter.
sections.why_notable: A highly ranked editor entry with a clear Rust-based, performance-oriented position in the developer-tool cluster.

sections.title: react/react
sections.description: The library for web and native user interfaces.
sections.why_notable: A large daily gain for a foundational UI library; one of three mature application frameworks in this snapshot.

sections.title: rust-lang/rust
sections.description: The Rust programming language, focused on reliable and efficient software.
sections.why_notable: A language-toolchain entry with meaningful daily gains, complemented by Rust-based Zed and Ruff in the same list.

sections.title: rails/rails
sections.why_notable: A mature full-stack framework among the top daily gainers, alongside React and Angular.

sections.title: prometheus/prometheus
sections.description: The Prometheus monitoring system and time-series database.
sections.why_notable: An infrastructure/observability counterpoint in the upper half of today's ranked list.

sections.title: angular/angular
sections.description: A platform for building web applications.
sections.why_notable: Completes the mature framework cluster with React and Rails, showing broad daily activity beyond AI tooling.

sections.title: etcd-io/etcd

sections.why_notable: A distributed-systems primitive that pairs with Prometheus and LZ4 in the infrastructure subset.

sections.why_notable: An efficient language-tooling project that supports the Rust/toolchain theme despite Python being its target language.

sections.title: livliv-dev/player
sections.description: A lightweight 2.5D character player for the web, with lip sync and webcam face tracking.
sections.why_notable: A recently created and actively pushed repository surfaced in the last-48-hour GitHub Search freshness check; its WebGL2 player supports multiple character formats and browser-side lip sync/face tracking.
sections.unique_caveat: Not present in today's GitHub Trending view, so no daily star-gain figure is available; its 908 stars are a snapshot, not evidence of sustained momentum.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- Agent skills and security workflows: Cloudflare/security-audit-skill, mattpocock/skills, and google/skills attracted large daily gains; they range from auditable security reviews to composable engineering practice and product-specific skills.
- Grounded agentic data: NVIDIA/auto-ontology centers semantic metadata, certified definitions, query validation, and provenance for data-connected agents.
- Editors and tooling: microsoft/vscode and zed-industries/zed headline editor interest; rust-lang/rust and astral-sh/ruff support a strong Rust/toolchain presence.
- Frameworks: react/react, angular/angular, and rails/rails show that established web application ecosystems remain prominent.
- Infrastructure: lz4/lz4, prometheus/prometheus, and etcd-io/etcd span compression, observability, and distributed coordination.
- Languages across the 15 entries: Rust 3, TypeScript 3, JavaScript 2, Python 2, Go 2, C 1, Ruby 1, Shell 1. The fresh LivLiv Player adds a smaller browser-graphics/creator-tool signal outside the Trending ranking.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is practical agent engineering rather than a new general-purpose model: skills, audit discipline, and grounded enterprise data access dominate the biggest gains. Mature editors, frameworks, and infrastructure projects remain part of the same snapshot, while LivLiv Player is an intriguing but not yet comparable fresh entrant.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository endpoints and default-branch commit endpoints; GitHub Search queries created:2026-11-04..2026-11-06 and pushed:2026-11-04..2026-11-06, each with stars:>100, to inspect fresh repositories. Trending gains are the stars-today values shown by GitHub's daily view. REST API total-star counts and default-branch SHAs were captured for every listed repository. livliv-dev/player was added from the recent search after reviewing its first-party README; it is not on the daily Trending view and has no daily gain figure. No prior-window data was gathered, so no Notable Shifts section is claimed.
